title: Runtime LTS initiative epic: branch, backport policy, CI/perf gates, and enterprise release process
creator: Talia Benson
description: Top-level epic to stand up an enterprise-friendly Long Term Support (LTS) channel for the serving runtime. Scope includes: branch/versioning, backport/change-control policy, perf regression gates, reproducible/artifact-signed releases, release notes taxonomy, and packaging/pinning for Private/Helm. Target: stable runtime baseline supported for 6–12+ months with predictable patch cadence (monthly + out-of-band security fixes).
body:
## Context / why
Enterprise Dedicated + Private customers are asking for a stable runtime line with slower-change semantics (kernel + scheduling stability) and auditable artifacts.

Recurring pain points:
- Incidents caused by “normal” mainline churn (perf variance, scheduler edge cases).
- Customers needing strong change control and predictable patch cadence.
- Private deployments requiring pinned versions + checksums/provenance for auditability.

This epic drives the LTS channel from branch strategy through GA-ready processes.

## Goals
1) Establish LTS branch strategy + versioning (e.g., `runtime-1.18-lts` with `1.18.x-lts` patches).
2) Publish explicit backport policy + risk rubric + approvals (security/Sev1/Sev2 eligibility).
3) Implement CI + perf regression gates for release branches; define waiver process.
4) Produce slower-change enterprise release notes (categorized changes, known issues, upgrade/rollback notes, compatibility matrix).
5) Deliver reproducible, verifiable artifacts (checksums/signing + provenance/SBOM story) for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
6) Define operational ownership: on-call/escalation expectations, incident→backport loop, comms to Support/CS/Sales.

## Non-goals
- Maintaining a divergent forked runtime architecture (must remain close to main).
- Guaranteeing feature parity with mainline.

## Milestones (phased plan)
### Phase 1 — decisions + docs (2–3 weeks)
- ADR: Branching + versioning scheme finalized and approved.
- Draft backport rubric and change-control/approvals.
- Release notes taxonomy/template for LTS patches.

### Phase 2 — implementation (4–6 weeks)
- Release branch CI workflow w/ deterministic build steps.
- Perf-canary gates integrated w/ defined thresholds + waiver workflow.
- Backport automation (labels + cherry-pick/backport helper).
- Artifact provenance + checksums/signing; SBOM generation or clear enterprise path.
- Private installer + Helm pinning support for LTS tags.

### Phase 3 — pilot (4 weeks)
- Pilot w/ 1–3 enterprise accounts.
- Cut first LTS patch and validate: gates, artifacts, notes, comms, and support workflow.

### Phase 4 — GA + steady state
- Docs published; Support/CS/Sales training.
- Monthly patch cadence established + OOB security patch playbook.
- Reporting: perf stability trends, incident-driven backports, and patch adoption.

## Definition of Done (epic)
- `runtime-1.18-lts` branch exists; tags + semantics documented.
- Backport policy published and enforced (labels, approvals, required tests/perf).
- CI gates: unit/integration + scheduler smoke tests + perf-canary summary required for release.
- Artifact verification supported: published checksums + provenance mapping to commits; signing keys and access controls documented.
- LTS release notes generated in “LTS mode” and meet enterprise template (incl. compatibility + known issues).
- Private installer and Helm can pin to specific LTS patch and rollback with validated artifacts.
- Support playbook and escalation path live; SLO dashboards/alerts for LTS traffic exist.
- At least 2 successful LTS patches cut with no Sev1 regressions introduced by backports.

## Key decisions captured so far
- LTS will be a release branch strategy (not a long-lived fork) with controlled cherry-picks.
- Backports require minimal diffs, targeted tests, and explicit perf validation (with waiver only via Release Eng + SRE sign-off).
- LTS defaults prioritize predictability (e.g., freezing kernel autotune defaults; disabling experimental batching heuristics if needed).

## Risks / watch-outs
- Perf gate flakiness due to runner contention; need capacity plan + rerun/waiver rules to avoid shipping blind.
- Backport correctness risk; avoid “fix bundles” and require tight scope.
- Signing keys access and CI secrets on release branches; reduce blast radius + audit access.

## Customer inputs driving urgency
- SUP-18477: latency regression after upgrading to runtime-1.18 → need pinning + stable baseline.
- SUP-18506: Private deployment needs version pinning + artifact checksums.
- Deal pressure: enterprise deals blocked on LTS commitment language (coordinate with AEs).

## Open questions
1) Support window defaults: 6 months vs 12 months for initial LTS line (proposal: 12 months for Dedicated/Private, with explicit EOL).
2) Minimum GPU/SKU coverage for perf gates on every patch (A100 + H100 always; L4 “best effort”?)
3) Mandatory vs optional patch policy: what triggers “mandatory upgrade” guidance (security, Sev1 correctness, data corruption risk).

## Latest updates
- 2025-03-22: Perf-canary workflows for release branches merged; defining final p95 regression thresholds + waiver template with SRE.
- 2025-03-18: Private installer pinning prototype validated in staging; checksum verification path confirmed; rollback UX needs documentation polish.
- 2025-03-10: Backport policy draft circulated; added explicit approvers: Runtime owner + Release Eng + (SRE for perf/rollout risk) + Security for CVEs.

## Next steps (this week)
- Lock threshold numbers for perf gate (p50/p95 + throughput) and publish waiver rubric.
- Finalize support/escalation expectations and mandatory patch criteria.
- Prep pilot account plan (Rachel/Liam) and success criteria for first patch rollout.
